messages:
incident-bot: PAGED oncall (P1) - Trace export errors: high rate of OTLP export failures to Honeycomb in us-west-2. Error rate > 40% for last 10m. Docs: https://runbooks.redwood/trace-export

amanda: acked. looking. attaching quick summary. seeing a spike of 5xx/429s from honeycomb exporter in the otel-collector logs.

sanjay: on way in. can you paste a couple of log lines?

amanda: sure — from otel-collector pod otel-collector-7d9f6:

```
2026-03-15T03:12:02Z ERROR exporter/honeycomb Export failed: Post "https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/trace": 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-15T03:12:03Z WARN exporter/retry Retrying export (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T03:12:04Z ERROR exporter/honeycomb Export failed: Post "https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/trace": 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z ERROR exporter/honeycomb Export failed: Post "https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/trace": context deadline exceeded
```

amanda: side note — metrics and spans still ingested locally; it's the remote export that's failing.

maria: jumping in. we just had a vendor alert from Honeycomb a few minutes ago about partial API degradation in us-west-2. link in vendor channel says rate-limited ingestion due to a downstream storage issue.

kevin: tagging product/support FYI — this will cause gaps in backend tracing for customer investigations. not customer-visible to end users (no API errors), but will affect our post-issue debugging.

amanda: impact assessment: traces not exported for ~40m window and counting. p50/p95 latency metrics unaffected. No user reports yet. recommended mitigation: enable local export buffering to object storage and flip to alternate export endpoint (eu fallback) for critical services.

sanjay: quick mitigation plan:
- throttle otel-collector exporters to reduce retry storm
- enable file-based persistence for the collector (filesystem queue) to avoid tail-drop
- temporarily route non-prod exports to honeycomb-eu endpoint to spread load
- alert Honeycomb support with our request ID and paste logs

amanda: executing steps 1 and 2 now. running kubectl exec into collector to tweak env.

```
# increase OTEL_EXPORTER_RETRY_MAX (temp) and enable PERSISTENCE_DIR
kubectl -n observability set env ds/otel-collector OTEL_EXPORTER_RETRY_MAX=8
kubectl -n observability set env ds/otel-collector PERSISTENCE_DIR=/var/otel/persist
```

amanda: update: changed envs and restarted collector DS. seeing fewer immediate 429s from our side, but vendor still returning 502s on some requests.

maria: Honeycomb support responded: "We are experiencing ingest backpressure due to compaction jobs; teams are throttling writes. We advise reducing client retry storms and using buffering." They've acknowledged our ticket #HB-12093 and will post updates.

ops-bot: ACTIONS recorded: mitigation-started by amanda at 03:30 UTC; ticket HB-12093 linked; severity P1 maintained.

kevin: good. can we get a rough ETA for full restore or for when exports will be green?

maria: vendor said they'll have a status update in ~30m. their timeline is uncertain.

amanda: additional note — enabling persistence increases disk usage on collectors; I've set retention to 24h and rotated path. we should triage disk usage after peak.

sanjay: for resiliency, I'm spinning up a temporary sidecar that writes a compressed trace bundle to S3 every 5m for critical services (hosted-api, routing). command:

```
kubectl -n hosted-api apply -f manifests/trace-sidecar-temp.yaml
# sidecar writes to s3://redwood-temp-trace-bucket/trace-backups/{{pod}}/{{ts}}.json.gz
```

amanda: thats in place. verifying a test trace wrote to bucket: SUCCESS.

maria: logging vendor update (03:58 UTC): "Reduced error rate; continuing throttling. Some customers will see elevated 429s. We are scaling compaction jobs now."

kevin: checklist for customer comms:
- no API outages, metrics ok, traces delayed/missing for ~40-80m window
- we are buffering and storing locally + S3 fallback for critical traces
- we opened vendor ticket HB-12093 and will update when vendor posts status

amanda: agreed. I'll prepare a short internal blurb for trust/security and support.

(04:15) incident-bot: Escalation timeline: P1 active — paging paused for stabilization.

sanjay: follow-up: I attached a quick query to detect missing traces trend:

```
# honeycomb query emulation: count(span_id) by minute where dataset="redwood-traces" and status!="ok"
```

we'll run it after vendor update.

maria: vendor updated (04:38 UTC): "Backpressure subsiding; we expect normal ingestion in 15-30m. Remaining throttles on heavy customers."

amanda: seeing export success rate climb to ~95% for new writes. backlog persists; collector is draining the persisted queue slowly.

kevin: impact update for ops notes: missing traces window expanded to 90m at worst. no known customer-impacting product errors. escalate to postmortem if total lost trace volume > 10% for any major customer.

ops-bot: NOTE created: incident/1875004321 - Trace export degradation to Honeycomb - assigned to observability team.

amanda: handing off to next oncall (sanjay) for night watch. I'll post incident summary + links to runbook + vendor ticket in #incidents.

sanjay: taking over. I'll keep vendor on chat and run the drain checklist. please add any followups to the incident doc.

kevin: thanks team. follow-ups: create postmortem, consider a durable cross-region export fallback, and add a retry/backoff tuning doc for collectors.

(05:07) incident-bot: HANDOFF recorded: amanda -> sanjay at 05:07 UTC. incident remains P1.

maria: noted for postmortem: root cause attributed to Honeycomb internal compaction/backpressure; our mitigations prevented customer-visible outages but caused potential trace loss and increased operational overhead.

amanda: closing my shift. all handoffs in the incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1875004321 (will add timeline + logs).

sanjay: will monitor and close when collector backlog drained and vendor confirms full restore. expected check at 06:00 UTC.

(06:10) sanjay: vendor confirms ingestion normal. collector persisted queue drained to <1% backlog. marking incident resolved; will file postmortem tomorrow.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 06:10 UTC — resolution: vendor-side compaction/backpressure; mitigations: collector persistence enabled, temporary S3 sidecar backups, throttle/retry tuning. Recommended action items: postmortem, add cross-region fallback, disk retention review.

kevin: solid work. closing thread. :thumbsup:
